title: The Power Behind Japan’s Takaichi Government
author: Jio Kamata
text:
Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae (second from right) poses with Nippon Ishin leaders Yoshimura Hirofumi (second from left) and Fujita Fumitake (far right) on Feb. 9, 2026, a day after the LDP’s sweeping election victory.
Credit: Facebook/ Nippon Ishin no Kai
On the day of a snap winter election – one that would ultimately end in a landslide victory for the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) – Takaichi  Sanae stood alongside two men. They were not members of her own party, but rather the two leaders of Nippon Ishin no Kai: Osaka Governor Yoshimura Hirofumi and Fujita Fumitake, who leads his party’s Diet delegation. Yet Yoshimura’s stump speech hardly sounded like one delivered by the leader of a different party. In fact, it barely sounded as though Takaichi herself belonged to the LDP.“We may not have the numbers. But we will never back down. We will not leave Takaichi-san standing alone,” Yoshimura declared. “We will not let Japan stand alone. We are determined to move Japan forward. That is the resolve with which we stand here today.”[...]
